summary: Spin-aware first bounce of a golf ball on compliant turf: the turf is an equivalent rigid surface tilted by theta_c, the Daish rigid-surface bounce (sliding, eq. 2, or rolling, eq. 3, chosen by mu_c of eq. 4) is applied in that tilted frame, and the hop length is the drag-free ballistic range of the rebound velocity on flat ground.

source.title: The run of a golf ball
source.equations: eqs. (2a)-(2b) sliding bounce, (3a)-(3b) rolling bounce, (4) critical friction mu_c, (5a)-(5b) restitution e, (6a)-(6b) and (7a)-(7b) frame rotation, (8) theta_c
source.accessed: 2026-11-24, full text read from the author's own copy of the published article

theta_c_ref_deg.where: eq. (8); best fit to Haake's one measured green impact (Section 2)

friction_mu.where: Section 2 (Daish's value for a ball sliding on a green) and Section 3, the value used for all of Penner's drive and iron runs

ball_radius_m.where: r of eqs. (3a) and (4); the radius the flight kernel uses (AeroBallProperties default)

limitations: theta_c of eq. (8) is a first-order law fitted to a single green impact (Penner, Section 2); e of eq. (5) was measured on relatively soft turf; mu = 0.40 is Daish's unmeasured green value. Penner integrates every bounce; this model takes only the first hop and leaves the rest of the run to the existing roll term, and the hop is drag-free over flat ground. At Penner's own Haake check point the printed eqs. (3), (6), (7) reproduce his mu_c = 0.29 and e = 0.14 but give a rebound of 4.16 m/s at 41.7 deg, not the 4.34 m/s at 34.1 deg he quotes. That quote needs a tilted-frame normal rebound of 2.82 m/s, which eq. (5) cannot produce at any normal speed up to 20 m/s (maximum 2.42 m/s), so the Haake figure is inconsistent with his printed equations; his quoted drive and 9-iron mu_c and bounce heights are reproduced by them and are the primary validation.
